subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What should OpenClaw core do when required startup SecretRef resolution through side-effecting exec providers repeatedly fails under a supervisor?
rationale: The current behavior is harmful, but bounded retry, fail-fast, crash-loop safe mode, provider-specific rate-limit handling, and delegated plugin caching make different security, availability, and operator-visibility tradeoffs that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Generic startup SecretRef resilience
options.body: Add an owner-approved generic policy such as bounded retry/backoff plus clear safe-mode or doctor recovery, with no vendor-specific 1Password behavior in core.

options.title: Delegate provider batching/caching
options.body: Keep core fail-fast and document ClawHub/plugin resolver patterns such as Varlock for backend batching, accepting that supervisor restart storms remain an operator-managed risk.

options.title: Narrow the linked PR
options.body: Use the linked PR only as a starting point, removing unrelated churn and requiring real 1Password or simulated exec-provider proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Generic startup SecretRef resilience
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved generic policy such as bounded retry/backoff plus clear safe-mode or doctor recovery, with no vendor-specific 1Password behavior in core.
